chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr from Muawiya said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever inclines therein to wrong unjustly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every injustice is heresy, and striking the servant without a fault is from that heresy.'

key_terms.إِلْحَاد: Heresy or deviation, here defined broadly as any act of injustice
key_terms.ضَرْبُ الْخَادِم: Striking the servant, used as an example of unjust heresy

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'ilhad' (heresy) in the context of injustice according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the semantic scope of 'ilhad' (heresy/deviation) beyond theological error to encompass all forms of unjust oppression (*zulm*). By citing the specific example of striking a servant without cause, he illustrates how physical tyranny constitutes a deviation from divine justice, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of servants and the broader ethical implications of the verse in Surah Al-Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Mjestic [22:25] and whoever shall incline therein to wrong unjustly. Heasws said: ‘Every injustice is heresy, and striking the servant regarding other than a fault is from that heresy’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘One who is found therein in deviation and injustice. . . .’ [22:24] He (the Imam) said, ‘All forms of injustice is deviation, causing harms to a servant without sin is of such deviation.”’
